claude.sample_unit: bariatric surgery FAQs (each answered by 3 LLMs, initial and simplified)

links.outcome: Reading grade level of institutional and initial LLM bariatric surgery patient education responses
links.effect: Institutional and initial LLM responses had poor readability, average reading levels 9th grade to college graduate; institutional FRE 48.1, GPT-3.5 initial 31.4, GPT-4 initial 42.7, Bard initial 56.3.
links.quote: All institutional and initial LLM responses had poor readability, with average reading levels ranging from 9th grade to college graduate.

links.outcome: Reading level of patient education materials versus 6th grade AMA recommendation
links.effect: Institutional PEMs and initial LLM responses exceeded the 6th grade level; institutional grade range 10th grade to college sophomore; simplified GPT-4 met the recommendation on only 2 of 6 instruments.
links.quote: Our analysis shows that institutional websites’ PEMs remain too complex for the public, falling short of the AMA recommendation that PEMs be written at a 6th grade level or below [ 13 ].

links.outcome: Readability change after prompting LLM to explain in simpler terms
links.effect: Simplified responses had significantly higher FRE and lower grade levels than initial for all LLMs (p<0.05); GPT-4 FRE 42.7 to 74.0, reading levels 6th to 9th grade.
links.quote: Simplified responses from GPT-3.5, GPT-4, and Bard received higher FRE scores, as well as lower grade levels across all instruments, compared to those of initial responses from GPT-3.5, GPT-4, and Bard, respectively ( p < 0.05) (Table 3 , Supplementary Table 7).

links.outcome: Accuracy and comprehensiveness of simplified versus initial LLM responses for lower-literacy readers
links.effect: Accuracy similar between initial and simplified; comprehensiveness maintained for GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 (92.4% equal) but 34.8% of Bard simplified responses were less comprehensive.
links.quote: However, 34.8% of simplified Bard responses were rated as less comprehensive than initial responses (Supplementary Table 8).

unlisted_practices: Prompting LLMs to simplify their responses on demand to improve patient education material readability

links.quote: Simplified responses from GPT-3.5, GPT-4, and Bard received higher FRE scores, as well as lower grade levels across all instruments, compared to those of initial responses from GPT-3.5, GPT-4, and Bard, respectively ( p < 0.05) (Table 3 , Supplementary Table 7).

links.effect: Institutional responses ranged 10th grade to college sophomore; initial GPT-3.5 college freshman to college graduate, GPT-4 12th to college senior, Bard 9th to college freshman.
links.quote: Our analysis shows poor readability among all institutions as well as initial LLM responses, where average reading levels ranged from 9th grade to college graduate.

links.outcome: Readability of bariatric surgery patient education materials
links.effect: Initial LLM responses ranged from 9th grade to college graduate (mean FRE 31.4 to 56.3), and institutional responses ranged from 10th grade to college sophomore (mean FRE 48.1).
links.quote: All institutional and initial LLM responses had poor readability, with average reading levels ranging from 9th grade to college graduate.

unlisted_practices: Conversational prompt to simplify initial responses ('Can you explain that in simpler terms?') to improve readability of patient education materials
